section.title: Safety hooks
section.subtitle: Put your own rules in front of a tool before it acts; external-command hooks (codex event names) live on this page too
group.external.title: External commands (codex event names)
group.external.description: Run external commands around model actions using codex's fourteen event names; the hook list lives in its own JSON file, while the switch, timeout and allowlist are here.
field.enabled.label: Enable safety hooks
field.enabled.help: While off, no rule and no script runs (the config is kept, so you can turn it back on anytime).
field.scriptFailClosed.label: Treat a failed script as a block
field.scriptFailClosed.help: A script that times out, will not start, or prints something unreadable is treated as “blocked”. Turn it off and it falls back to “a script that cannot run is no hook at all” — harder to trace when something goes wrong, so leave it on.
field.scriptTimeoutMs.label: Default script timeout (ms)
field.scriptTimeoutMs.help: A hook script is a gate, not a background job, so it is killed past this time. Range {min}–{max} ms.
field.autoAccept.label: Run new scripts without asking
field.autoAccept.help: This hands an “execute arbitrary code” entry point straight to this config file. Leave it off unless you are using it for automation.
field.problems.label: The config has problems
field.problems.help: Broken entries were skipped; the other rules still apply.
field.rules.label: Rules in the UI
field.rules.text: {count} registered (200 at most). A rule only looks at which tool, which field and which pattern matches — it starts no process.
field.ruleId.label: Pick a rule
field.ruleId.option.none: (no rules yet — add one with the four boxes below)
field.ruleEnabled.label: Enable the selected rule
field.ruleDelete.label: Delete the selected rule
field.ruleTool.label: New rule: which tools
field.ruleTool.help: * covers every tool; separate several with a pipe or a comma, and tool names ignore case.
field.ruleField.label: New rule: which field
field.rulePattern.label: New rule: what counts as a match (regex, case-insensitive)
field.rulePattern.help: Matches any part of the regex (the whole string need not match). At most {max} characters; a broken regex is reported right away.
field.ruleAction.label: New rule: what happens on a match
field.ruleReason.label: New rule: the reason for the model and the user
field.ruleReason.placeholder: A force push overwrites other people's commits; the user must confirm
field.ruleReason.help: This sentence appears verbatim in the tool result that was blocked, and the model uses it to change course. At most {max} characters.
field.ruleAdd.label: Add to the rule list
field.selectedRule.label: Which one
field.selectedRule.text.empty: The rule list is still empty
field.scripts.label: Script hooks
field.scripts.text: {count} registered (50 at most). A script gets the JSON of this call on stdin and answers with exit code 2 or JSON on stdout.
field.scriptId.label: Pick a script
field.scriptId.option.none: (no scripts yet — add one with the three boxes below)
field.scriptEnabled.label: Enable the selected script
field.scriptState.label: State of this script
field.scriptTrust.label: Approve this script
field.scriptTrust.renew.label: Approve the current contents again
field.scriptTrust.help: Approving records the script file's modification time: change the contents and this hook stops running until it is approved again.
field.scriptUntrust.label: Withdraw approval
field.scriptDelete.label: Delete the selected script
field.scriptEvent.label: New script: which event
field.scriptMatcher.label: New script: which tools only (regex)
field.scriptMatcher.help: Only the “before a tool acts” and “after a tool finishes” events look at this box; every other event runs each time.
field.scriptCommand.label: New script: command
field.scriptCommand.help: Run through the shell, so arguments and pipes both work. Credentials are stripped from the child process environment.
field.scriptAdd.label: Add to the script list
field.recent.label: Recent hits
field.configFile.label: Config file
field.configFile.help: Rules and scripts both live here; editing the file by hand works too, and the next tool call uses the new contents.
field.trustFile.label: Script approval list
field.policyFile.label: How this differs from the command risk rules
field.policyFile.help: That file decides how dangerous a command is (bash command text only, and it can allow); the hooks here cover every tool and can only tighten, never loosen. To loosen something, write a prefix rule in that file.
field.externalEnabled.label: Enable external-command hooks
field.externalEnabled.help: While off, none of these hooks run (the hook config file is kept, so you can turn it back on anytime).
field.externalConfigPath.label: Hook config file
field.externalConfigPath.help: codex-shaped JSON: `{ "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "node guard.js", "timeout": 5 }] }] } }`. timeout is in seconds.
field.externalTimeoutMs.label: Default hook timeout (ms)
field.externalTimeoutMs.help: Used when a hook does not set its own timeout. Range {min}–{max} ms.
field.externalFailClosed.label: Treat a failed hook as a block
field.externalFailClosed.help: Off by default, same as codex: a hook blocks this call only by exiting with code 2 (and writing the reason to stderr); a timeout, a failure to start or a non-zero exit just leaves a notice. Turn it on and those cases block as well.
field.externalCommandAllowlist.label: Command allowlist
field.externalCommandAllowlist.placehold: Empty = no limit; for example node, uv
field.externalCommandAllowlist.help: When filled in, only hooks whose first word is on the list run (`node` allows `node guard.js` but not `nodejs-evil`). A hook blocked here counts as “did not run”; whether that blocks is decided by the switch above.
field.externalCapabilities.label: Wiring status of the fourteen events ({unwired} not wired)
field.externalCapabilities.help: Events marked “not wired” have no extension point in dsc today, so hooks configured for them never run; the reasons are in the block below.
field.externalLoaded.label: Loaded external-command hooks
field.externalLoaded.empty: (no hooks in the config file yet)
field.externalProblems.label: External hooks that are not wired or not in effect
field.externalProblems.help: Broken entries were skipped; the other hooks still apply.
field.externalFile.label: Config file actually read
save.notNumberMs: Enter a number of milliseconds here.
save.configPathEmpty: The hook config file path cannot be empty.
save.ruleEmpty: The rule list is empty, so there is no rule to enable or disable.
save.scriptEmpty: The script list is empty, so there is no script to enable or disable.
save.unknownKey: This section has no such setting: {key}
action.ruleAdded: Rule added to the list (enabled by default)
action.scriptAddedAuto: Script added. Because “run new scripts without asking” is on, it runs right away
action.scriptAdded: Script added, but it has not run yet: click “Approve this script” in the details to activate it
action.scriptDeleted: Script deleted, and its approval was withdrawn with it
action.scriptTrusted: Approved; this script runs from now on
action.scriptUntrusted: Approval withdrawn: this script will not run until it is approved again
action.unknownName: This section has no such button: {name}
